items: Not all headaches are created equal, and certain patterns demand neurological investigation. Recognizing the difference between a benign headache and one requiring urgent care can be lifesaving. At Palamu Neuro & Eye Care, our specialists are committed to delivering this high standard of care locally in Medininagar.
In Palamu: Thunderclap headache — reaches maximum intensity within 60 seconds and can indicate subarachnoid hemorrhage, a life-threatening emergency.
Headaches that consistently wake you from sleep, are most severe in the early morning, or are accompanied by projectile vomiting — raise concern for raised intracranial pressure from a mass lesion.
New onset headaches in a person over 50 — warrant evaluation for giant cell arteritis, which can cause irreversible blindness if untreated.

Strictly unilateral headaches always on the same side, with autonomic symptoms such as eye redness, tearing, nasal congestion, or eyelid drooping — suggest cluster headaches or other trigeminal autonomic cephalalgias.
Headache with fever and neck stiffness — requires urgent evaluation for meningitis.
A significant change in the pattern, frequency, or severity of a previously stable headache disorder (e.g., migraine becoming daily when it was once monthly) — should prompt a neurology consultation.

Disorders of movement and coordination often provide early clues to neurological disease. Subtle changes in how you move can be the first indication of an underlying condition. At Palamu Neuro & Eye Care, our specialists are committed to delivering this high standard of care locally in Medininagar.
In Palamu: Resting tremor — a pill-rolling motion of the thumb and forefinger that diminishes with voluntary movement, hallmark of Parkinson's disease.
Intention tremor — worsens as the hand approaches a target, suggesting cerebellar dysfunction.
Bradykinesia (slowness in initiating and executing movements) with rigidity and a shuffling gait with reduced arm swing — the classic triad of parkinsonism.
Sudden unprovoked jerking movements of the limbs — may represent myoclonus or seizure activity.
Ataxia — unsteady wide-based gait, difficulty with tandem walking, and dysmetria on finger-to-nose testing, pointing to cerebellar pathology from stroke, multiple sclerosis, or hereditary ataxias.
Chorea — involuntary dance-like movements flowing from one body part to another, seen in Huntington's disease and Sydenham chorea.
Progressive muscle stiffness and painful spasms, particularly in the back and lower limbs — characteristic of stiff person syndrome.

content.text: Any new involuntary movement, persistent clumsiness, or frequent unexplained falls should be evaluated by a neurologist.

sections.heading: Sensory Changes: Numbness, Tingling, and Vision

items: Sensory disturbances are among the most common neurological complaints and can range from benign to ominous. The key distinguishing factors are the distribution, onset speed, and associated symptoms. At Palamu Neuro & Eye Care, our specialists are committed to delivering this high standard of care locally in Medininagar.

In Palamu: Peripheral neuropathy — symmetrical stocking-glove pattern of numbness, burning, or tingling beginning in the toes and slowly ascending. Commonly associated with diabetes, vitamin B12 deficiency, alcohol use, or chemotherapy.
Sudden unilateral numbness involving the face, arm, and leg — a classic stroke presentation requiring immediate emergency care.
Single dermatome numbness, often radiating around the chest in a band-like pattern — suggests radiculopathy from a herniated disc.
Transient sensory symptoms in multiple limbs that evolve over days, particularly in a young adult — may be the first episode of multiple sclerosis.
Optic neuritis — pain with eye movement and loss of central vision, often with washed-out color perception. Another possible first manifestation of multiple sclerosis.
Lhermitte's sign — an electric shock sensation down the spine and limbs upon flexing the neck forward, occurring with cervical spinal cord lesions.
Cognitive changes exist on a spectrum from normal age-related slowing to pathological decline, and distinguishing the two is crucial for timely intervention.

Normal aging may bring occasional word-finding difficulty and slower processing speed, but pathological cognitive decline involves more disruptive changes. At Palamu Neuro & Eye Care, our specialists are committed to delivering this high standard of care locally in Medininagar.
In Palamu: Forgetting recently learned information and repeatedly asking the same questions.
Increasingly relying on memory aids or family members for tasks one previously managed independently.
New difficulty with planning, problem-solving, or managing finances.
Getting lost in familiar neighborhoods and inability to recognize familiar faces.
Significant personality changes: new apathy, social withdrawal, disinhibition, or paranoia — red flags for Alzheimer's disease and frontotemporal dementia.
Fluctuating cognition with visual hallucinations, REM sleep behavior disorder, and parkinsonism — suggests Lewy body dementia.

Rapidly progressive cognitive decline over weeks to months, often with myoclonus and gait disturbance — a medical emergency requiring evaluation for Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease or autoimmune encephalitis.

content.text: Any cognitive change that interferes with the ability to perform daily activities independently warrants a comprehensive neurological and neuropsychological assessment.

sections.heading: When to Seek Emergency Neurological Care

items: Certain neurological symptoms require immediate emergency care because the window for effective treatment is measured in minutes to hours. At Palamu Neuro & Eye Care, our specialists are committed to delivering this high standard of care locally in Medininagar.

content.title: Remember BE FAST for Stroke
content.text: Balance loss, Eyesight changes, Facial drooping, Arm weakness, Speech difficulty — Time to call for help. If any of these appear suddenly, go to the nearest emergency department immediately.

items: In Palamu: Status epilepticus — a seizure lasting more than five minutes or recurrent seizures without regaining consciousness between them. A life-threatening emergency.
Sudden severe headache with altered consciousness, neck stiffness, and photophobia — demands urgent evaluation for subarachnoid hemorrhage or meningitis.

Acute spinal cord compression from trauma, tumor, or infection — presenting with new bilateral limb weakness, sensory level on the trunk, and bladder or bowel dysfunction. A surgical emergency that can result in permanent paralysis if not decompressed within hours.
At Palamu Neuro & Eye Care, we guide patients on recognizing these emergencies and provide prompt outpatient follow-up care after emergency treatment has been initiated.

faqs.question: How do I know if my headache is serious enough to see a neurologist?
faqs.answer: You should see a neurologist like Dr. Yuvraj Lahre if your headaches are severe enough to interfere with work or daily activities, occur more than twice a week, do not respond to over-the-counter pain relievers, are accompanied by neurological symptoms such as visual aura, numbness, or speech difficulty, or represent a significant change from your usual headache pattern. A headache that reaches peak intensity within seconds, wakes you from sleep, or is accompanied by fever and neck stiffness requires emergency evaluation. Our team at Palamu Neuro & Eye Care is dedicated to providing these advanced services locally in Medininagar, Jharkhand.

faqs.question: Is occasional numbness in my hands something to worry about?
faqs.answer: Occasional numbness in the hands can be benign, such as compression from sleeping in an awkward position, or it may indicate an underlying condition. Carpal tunnel syndrome typically causes numbness in the thumb, index, and middle fingers, often waking you at night. If numbness persists, recurs frequently, spreads to other areas, affects both hands symmetrically, or is accompanied by weakness, it warrants neurological evaluation. Dr. Yuvraj Lahre can perform nerve conduction studies at Palamu Neuro & Eye Care to determine whether a neuropathy or nerve entrapment is present and recommend appropriate treatment.

faqs.question: What is the difference between normal forgetfulness and dementia?
faqs.answer: Normal age-related forgetfulness includes occasionally misplacing items, momentarily forgetting an appointment, or struggling to recall a word but remembering it later. Dementia involves memory loss that disrupts daily life, such as getting lost in familiar places, inability to manage finances or medications, repeatedly asking the same questions, and significant personality or behavioral changes. The rule of thumb is that if cognitive changes interfere with the ability to complete daily activities independently, a neurological evaluation is warranted. Early diagnosis allows access to treatments that can slow progression. Our team at Palamu Neuro & Eye Care is dedicated to providing these advanced services locally in Medininagar, Jharkhand.

faqs.question: Can stress and anxiety cause neurological symptoms?
faqs.answer: Yes, stress and anxiety can manifest with genuine physical neurological symptoms including tension headaches, muscle twitching, tremors, dizziness, brain fog, and tingling sensations, often through mechanisms involving hyperventilation and heightened sympathetic nervous system activity. However, these same symptoms can also indicate organic neurological disease, and distinguishing between the two requires expert evaluation. A neurologist like Dr. Yuvraj Lahre performs a thorough clinical assessment and, when appropriate, diagnostic tests to rule out structural or degenerative causes before attributing symptoms to stress. In many cases, a combination of stress management and medical treatment yields the best results. Our team at Palamu Neuro & Eye Care is dedicated to providing these advanced services locally in Medininagar, Jharkhand.

hero.subtitle: Simple daily habits and informed choices can protect your vision for a lifetime. Discover evidence-based eye care strategies from our retina specialist at Palamu Neuro & Eye Care, serving Medininagar and Jharkhand.

items: Maintaining healthy eyes requires consistent daily habits that many people overlook. Here are the most important ones to incorporate into your routine: At Palamu Neuro & Eye Care, our specialists are committed to delivering this high standard of care locally in Medininagar.

In Palamu: Follow the 20-20-20 rule when using screens: every 20 minutes, look at something 20 feet away for at least 20 seconds. This relaxes the ciliary muscles responsible for focusing and reduces accommodative strain.
Blink consciously and frequently — the average blink rate drops from 15–20 blinks per minute to as low as 5–7 during screen use, leading to tear film instability and dry eye symptoms.

Practice good eyelid hygiene: wash your hands before touching your eyes, remove all eye makeup before sleeping, and replace mascara and eyeliner every three months to prevent bacterial buildup. Never share eye cosmetics or eye drops.
Stay well hydrated — the tear film is largely water-based, and dehydration contributes to dry eye symptoms.
Avoid rubbing your eyes, which can introduce bacteria, worsen allergies, and even contribute to keratoconus, a progressive thinning of the cornea.
Wear appropriate protective eyewear during sports, home improvement projects, gardening, and any activity that poses a risk of ocular injury.

These small daily commitments build a strong foundation for lifelong eye health. At Palamu Neuro & Eye Care, our specialists are committed to delivering this high standard of care locally in Medininagar.

sections.heading: Nutrition for Eye Health: Key Nutrients and Foods

items: Diet plays a fundamental role in preserving vision and reducing the risk of age-related eye diseases. Each nutrient below targets a specific aspect of ocular health: At Palamu Neuro & Eye Care, our specialists are committed to delivering this high standard of care locally in Medininagar.

In Palamu: Lutein and zeaxanthin — carotenoids concentrated in the macula that act as natural blue light filters and antioxidants. Rich sources include spinach, kale, collard greens, egg yolks, corn, and orange bell peppers.

Omega-3 fatty acids (DHA and EPA) — support retinal structure and reduce dry eye inflammation. Found in salmon, sardines, mackerel, and tuna. Vegetarian sources include flaxseeds, chia seeds, and walnuts (ALA precursor form).
Vitamin C — a potent antioxidant that slows cataract progression and supports corneal health. Found in citrus fruits, strawberries, bell peppers, and broccoli.
Vitamin E — protects retinal cell membranes from oxidative damage. Found in almonds, sunflower seeds, and wheat germ.
Zinc — facilitates vitamin A transport from the liver to the retina for melanin production. Abundant in legumes, nuts, seeds, and whole grains.
Beta-carotene — converted to vitamin A, essential for night vision and corneal maintenance. Found in carrots, sweet potatoes, and pumpkin.

content.title: Clinical Evidence
content.text: The AREDS and AREDS2 studies demonstrated that a specific combination of these nutrients can slow the progression of moderate to advanced age-related macular degeneration.

sections.heading: Screen Time and Digital Eye Strain Management

items: Digital eye strain, also known as computer vision syndrome, affects over 60% of people who use digital devices for more than two hours daily. The condition arises from a combination of sustained near focusing, reduced blink rate, glare, and poor ergonomics. At Palamu Neuro & Eye Care, our specialists are committed to delivering this high standard of care locally in Medininagar.

In Palamu: Position your screen at arm's length with the top at or just below eye level so you gaze slightly downward — this promotes a more relaxed eyelid position and reduces exposed ocular surface area.
Adjust ambient lighting to match screen brightness; the screen should not be the brightest or darkest object in the room. Use a matte screen filter if glare is unavoidable.
Enable night mode or blue light reduction settings during evening hours — excessive blue light exposure suppresses melatonin secretion and disrupts sleep.
Consider computer glasses with an anti-reflective coating optimized for your typical viewing distance.
Use preservative-free artificial tears to maintain the tear film during prolonged screen sessions.

If you experience persistent eye strain, schedule a comprehensive eye examination — an uncorrected refractive error or accommodative dysfunction may be the underlying cause. At Palamu Neuro & Eye Care, our specialists are committed to delivering this high standard of care locally in Medininagar.

sections.heading: Protecting Your Eyes from UV and Injury

items: Ultraviolet radiation from sunlight is a cumulative risk factor for multiple eye conditions. Chronic UV exposure accelerates cataract formation, contributes to pterygium (a fleshy growth on the conjunctiva that can encroach upon the cornea), increases the risk of macular degeneration, and can cause photokeratitis — essentially a sunburn of the cornea — after intense short-term exposure. At Palamu Neuro & Eye Care, our specialists are committed to delivering this high standard of care locally in Medininagar.
In Palamu: Wear sunglasses that block 99–100% of both UVA and UVB rays year-round — UV penetrates cloud cover. Wrap-around styles provide additional protection from peripheral rays.
A wide-brimmed hat reduces UV reaching the eyes by up to 50%.
Polarized lenses reduce glare from reflective surfaces such as water, snow, and roads, improving visual comfort and safety.
For prescription glasses wearers, photochromic lenses that darken in sunlight offer convenient UV protection.

Beyond UV, physical eye protection is equally critical — over 90% of eye injuries are preventable with appropriate protective eyewear. Polycarbonate lenses with ANSI Z87.1-rated frames should be worn during sports like squash, badminton, and cricket, and during home activities involving hammering, drilling, or chemical use. At Palamu Neuro & Eye Care, our specialists are committed to delivering this high standard of care locally in Medininagar.

content.text: At Palamu Neuro & Eye Care, we educate every patient on protective measures tailored to their lifestyle and occupation.

sections.heading: The Importance of Regular Eye Exams

items: Many sight-threatening eye diseases are asymptomatic in their early stages, making regular comprehensive eye examinations the single most important health habit for preserving vision. At Palamu Neuro & Eye Care, our specialists are committed to delivering this high standard of care locally in Medininagar.

In Palamu: Glaucoma — the second leading cause of blindness worldwide, called the "silent thief of sight" because peripheral vision loss occurs so gradually that patients don't notice until irreversible damage has occurred.

Diabetic retinopathy — the leading cause of preventable blindness in working-age adults, producing no symptoms in early stages, yet treatable with laser and anti-VEGF injections to prevent severe vision loss.
Age-related macular degeneration — may begin with subtle changes detectable only through dilated fundus examination and optical coherence tomography.

Systemic conditions — hypertension and elevated cholesterol produce characteristic retinal blood vessel changes visible during an eye exam, sometimes prompting the first diagnosis. Brain tumors, autoimmune conditions, and thyroid eye disease can also be detected.

The general recommendation is a dilated eye exam every 1–2 years for adults aged 40–64, and annually for those 65 and older. At Palamu Neuro & Eye Care, our specialists are committed to delivering this high standard of care locally in Medininagar.

content.text: At Palamu Neuro & Eye Care, Dr. Dibya Prabha provides thorough examinations with advanced imaging to catch these silent conditions before they compromise your vision.

faqs.question: Do carrots really improve eyesight?
faqs.answer: Carrots are rich in beta-carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A. Vitamin A is essential for the production of rhodopsin, a pigment in the retina that enables vision in low-light conditions. While eating carrots supports overall eye health and prevents vitamin A deficiency that could lead to night blindness and corneal damage, they will not improve vision beyond your baseline or reduce your need for glasses. A balanced diet including dark leafy greens, colorful vegetables, fatty fish, and nuts provides a broader spectrum of eye-protective nutrients. For specific concerns about your diet and eye health, consult Dr. Dibya Prabha at Palamu Neuro & Eye Care.

faqs.question: How can I reduce eye strain from working on a computer all day?
faqs.answer: To reduce computer-related eye strain, apply the 20-20-20 rule consistently: every 20 minutes, look at something at least 20 feet away for 20 seconds. Position your monitor slightly below eye level at arm's length. Adjust brightness and contrast to comfortable levels, and eliminate screen glare by repositioning lights or using a matte filter. Use preservative-free artificial tears to combat dryness from reduced blinking. Ensure your glasses or contact lens prescription is up to date and optimized for your typical screen distance. Consider computer glasses with blue light filtering and anti-reflective coating. If symptoms persist despite these measures, schedule a comprehensive eye exam at Palamu Neuro & Eye Care, as an underlying refractive or binocular vision issue may be contributing.

faqs.question: Are over-the-counter eye drops safe for daily use?
faqs.answer: Not all over-the-counter eye drops are suitable for daily use. Drops marketed for redness relief contain vasoconstrictors such as naphazoline or tetrahydrozoline that temporarily shrink blood vessels but can cause rebound redness with prolonged use, creating a cycle of dependency. Preservative-containing artificial tears can irritate the ocular surface if used more than four times daily because preservatives like benzalkonium chloride are toxic to corneal epithelial cells. For frequent use, choose preservative-free artificial tears in single-dose vials. Always check the expiry date and avoid touching the dropper tip to any surface to prevent contamination. Dr. Dibya Prabha can recommend the most appropriate formulation for your specific type of dry eye at Palamu Neuro & Eye Care.

faqs.question: At what age should I start getting regular eye exams?
faqs.answer: Eye examinations should begin in infancy, with the first comprehensive exam between 6 and 12 months of age, followed by exams at age 3 and before starting school. School-age children should be examined every one to two years. Adults aged 20 to 39 should have at least one comprehensive exam in their twenties and two in their thirties, more frequently if they wear contact lenses or have risk factors like diabetes or a family history of eye disease. From age 40 onward, exams every one to two years are recommended because the risk of glaucoma, cataract, and age-related macular degeneration begins to rise. Adults 65 and older should have annual comprehensive eye exams. These are general guidelines; Dr. Dibya Prabha personalizes screening intervals based on your individual risk profile.
